strings.shelf.collectionsBlurb: the game proper — every level with a world best to beat
strings.shelf.tutorialsBlurb: short packs that teach the objects and the tricks
strings.shelf.walkthroughsBlurb: one hard level of the original, shown part-solved
strings.note.lasertank: The original file — the game as Jim Kindley shipped it, and still where everyone starts.
strings.note.challenge1: For when the original runs out. Five more full-length files, no gentler and no easier.
strings.note.challenge2: The second of the five that pick up where the original file ends.
strings.note.challenge3: The third of the five that pick up where the original file ends.
strings.note.challenge4: The fourth of the five that pick up where the original file ends.
strings.note.challenge5: The last of the five, and the one still filling up — new levels land here first.
strings.note.beginner1: Levels the other files turned down for being too easy, which makes this the place to learn.
strings.note.beginner2: More of the same: the gentle end of the corpus, and the one to hand a child.
strings.note.sokoban1: Push-the-block puzzles in the spirit of Sokoban, with a tank and a laser where the warehouse keeper was.
strings.note.sokoban2: The second Sokoban file. Same idea, less room to turn around in.
strings.note.gary1: Gary's series, lifted out of the main files: one idea at a time, turned over until it is finished.
strings.note.gary2: The rest of Gary's, and the smallest of the thirteen.
strings.note.special1: The offcuts — levels the other files turned away for being too long, too alike or too strange.
strings.note.objects: One level per object, each with its solution recorded: what every tile in the game does.
strings.note.tutorPlaybacks: The beginner's course, every level with its solution recorded. Start here if the objects are new.
strings.note.tutor: The trick specification: one level per undocumented behaviour, each explained in its own hint. Most are bugs the author left in on purpose.
strings.note.rotary: Rotating mirrors and nothing else, every level with its playback — the one object worth a file of its own.
strings.note.tricks: Levels built out of the Tutor tricks, made to be watched rather than fought.
strings.note.pono: Mau's levels on Pono's trick: how to cross thin ice without breaking it.
strings.note.l40: Level 40 of the original, “Down the Drain”, opened out stage by stage. The author: “It took me 4 hours to do this one.”
strings.note.triangles: Level 149 of the original, “The 4 Triangles”, broken into stages.
strings.note.telekinesis: Level 173 of the original, “Telekinesis”, with the positions that give it away.
strings.note.inchworm: Level 179 of the original, “Being an Inchworm”, with the position that gives it away.
